Endogeneity    Definition

Endogenous issue





Definition:

    endogeneity broadly refers to situations in which an explanatory variable is
     correlated with the error term, that is:

                              Cov(x, u) ̸= 0



Consequence:
    Cov(x, u) ̸= 0 ⇒E(u|x) ̸= 0.
       ˆβ1 is a biased and inconsistent estimator.





            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                            November 18, 2024           4 / 15

Endogeneity    Sources of endogeneity

Sources of endogeneity



Omitted variable bias

       It occurs when a model leaves out a confounding variable that is a
     determinant of the dependent variable y and correlated with included
     independent variables x.


Measurement error of explanatory variable x

    x is measured with error, and the error becomes a component of the random
      error term.


Simultaneity (reversed causality)

    The change of X is a cause of the change of Y while the change of Y is also a
     cause of the change of X.

Instrumental Variable    Definition and properties

Definition and properties





Instrumental variable

       is an observable variable z correlated with the endogenous explanatory
     variable x but uncorrelated with the random error u.

       is an exogenous variable z but not an omitted variable in terms of the model:
    y = β0 + β1x + u


Required properties of z.

    Instrument exogeneity: Cov(z, u) = 0
    Instrument relevance: Cov(z, x) ̸= 0





            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                            November 18, 2024           7 / 15

Instrumental Variable    IV estimation of β1: 2SLS

2-stage least squares


2SLS is used to obtain the IV estimator ˆβ1,IV
      First stage: isolate the part of x that is correlated with the random error u.
     (regress x on z using OLS):

                                 xi = π0 + π1zi + vi

    Second stage: replace xi by the predicted value ˆxi and regress y on ˆx:

                                     yi = β0 + β1ˆxi + ui



IV estimator:
                   Pni=1(zi −z)(yi −y)                               ˆβ1,IV =
                   Pni=1(zi −z)(xi −x)

Instrumental Variable  β1 under IV estimation

True value of the β1 under IV estimation


For a model with an endogenous explanatory variable x:

                            y = β0 + β1x + u

Suppose we have a valid instrument variable z.


According to the instrument exogeneity: Cov(z, u) = 0, we have:

                   Cov(z, u) = Cov(z, y −β0 −β1x) = 0

                           cov(z, y) −β1cov(z, x) = 0

According to the instrument relevance: Cov(z, x) ̸= 0, we yield:

                                 Cov(z, y)
                             β1 =
                                 Cov(z, x)

Instrumental Variable    Checking instrument relevance

Weak instrumental variable test: F-test


Consider the following model with 1 endogenous variable x1 and k −1 exogenous
variables x2, · · · , xk, suppose we have m instruments:

                          yi = β0 + β1x1i + · · · + βkxki + ui

Test for the null hypothesis with multiple restrictions:


                  H0 : π1 = π2 = · · · = πm = 0

where π1, π2, · · · , πm are the coefficients from the first-stage regression model:

          x1i = π0 + π1z1i + · · · + πmzmi + α1x2i + · · · + αk−1xki + vi

Rule of Thumb:
       If F-statistic F(m, n −m −k) > 10, the instruments are not week.
    Note: all exogenous variables must be included in first-stage regression,
     otherwise, estimators may be inconsistent.



            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                            November 18, 2024          11 / 15

Instrumental Variable    Checking instrument exogeneity

Overidentification test: J-test


Consider the same model on page 11, we use 2SLS estimators to obtain the
predicted ˆyi, and get the residuals ˆui = yi −ˆyi.


Test for the null hypothesis with multiple restrictions:

                  H0 : θ1 = θ2 = · · · = θm = 0

where θ1, θ2, · · · , θm are the coefficients from the regression model:

                 ˆui = θ0 + θ1z1i + · · · + θmzmi + δ1x2i + · · · + δk−1xki + ϵi

Rejection rule:
    J −statistic = m · F ∼χ2m−r > cα.(Seeing P-value is an alternative way)
  m is the number of instruments, r is the number of endogenous variables.

    There is no valid test if m = r or m < r.
     Fail to reject H0 does not mean accept!

Stata Commands for IV Estimation

Syntax

 If we have one endogenous variable x2 and two IVs z1, z2, we can use the
following syntax:

                           ivregress 2sls y x1 (x2 = z1 z2)

 If we have multiple endogenous variables x2, x3 and multiple IVs z1, z2, z3, we
can use the following syntax:

                        ivregress 2sls y x1 (x2 x3 = z1 z2 z3)

Then, carry out statistical inference after regression.

Check for instrument relevance:

                                  estat firststage,all

Check for instrument exogeneity:

                                     estat overid
